text:
maria: Quick follow-up after the RFC — I think we need a tiny 'clean-room' doc that spells where auth translation lives for hosted <> dedicated <> private. short q: control-plane translate or edge-sidecar?
oleg: leaning control-plane for hosted->dedicated translation. single place to audit and rotate creds.
sam: control-plane has good audit but adds an extra network hop for private paths. worried about latency-sensitive sync calls. :thinking_face:
priya: if we keep it in control-plane we must ensure the control-plane can reach customer VPCs or provide a transit-only agent. otherwise private loses meaning.
maria: good point. alternative: keep token translation at the runtime edge (sidecar) for private, control-plane for hosted. that splits logic but keeps latency for private low.
ochris: split-surface ok but ops complexity skyrockets — two code paths to maintain. also more places to leak secrets.
sam: what if we define a minimal contract: "Translate(token) -> {claims, tenant_id}" with explicit blinding rules. implement contract either in control-plane or sidecar. runtime must declare capabilities.
priya: +1 on capability manifest. maybe a small policy file in manifest: `auth.translation: controlplane|sidecar|none` and `auth.mode: passthrough|reissue`
maria: example manifest snippet I sketched:
```
kind: DeploymentManifest
metadata:
  tenant: acme
auth:
  translation: sidecar
  mode: reissue
```
oleg: having explicit flags makes rollback safer. if sidecar fails we can flip to control-plane reissue. but need a safe circuit-breaker for cross-mode fallbacks.
sam: fallback rules: prefer local sidecar, on failure try control-plane if policy allows, else return 503. keep failures observable.
priya: telemetry: add per-tenant counters for `translation.success`, `translation.fallback`, `translation.latency_ms`. tie to billing/alerts.
ochris: one more tradeoff: KMS access. sidecar needs transient keys or a token to reissue — requiring HSM access on customer network. control-plane can reissue without direct KMS in customer network.
maria: ops suggestion: for Private we support a 'proxy-mode' where control-plane only brokers blinded assertions (no raw keys) and sidecar performs final reissue. reduces surface for control-plane.
oleg: sounds promising. can we prototype a state machine: SIDEcar_OK -> use_sidecar, SIDEcar_FAIL & ALLOW_CP -> controlplane, else -> error. keep circuit breaker window 30s.
priya: I'll add manifest fields + telemetry proposal to the RFC doc. who wants to own a tiny prototype?
sam: I can spin up a quick prototype on monday. will simulate latency and failure modes.
ochris: I'll review the security implications and KMS flows.
deploy-bot: deployment started for sandbox/prototype on us-west-2 (build 2026.03.23-042).
maria: thanks all — main outcome: agree to codify a capability manifest, explicit fallback rules, and a prototype of sidecar/control-plane combo. tiny doc follow-up incoming. :thumbsup:
